create.name: Kumu Ramsay Taum
create.bio:
Kumu Ramsay Taum, a Native Hawaiian cultural practitioner and teacher, founded the Life Enhancement Institute of the Pacific. Trained and mentored by respected kūpuna (elders), he practises and teaches hoʻoponopono, the Hawaiian process of forgiveness and reconciliation, along with lomi haha (body alignment) and the Hawaiian martial art Kaihewalu Lua. After his schooling at The Kamehameha Schools he spent time at the US Air Force Academy, and he later earned a public administration degree at the University of Southern California.

As a speaker, adviser and facilitator he brings Hawaiian values such as aloha, pono and kuleana into business, tourism, planning and community life. He offers hoʻoponopono sessions for groups and individuals, in-person immersions in Lua, hoʻoponopono and the Aloha Way, and talks for conferences, churches and TEDx. His course on The Shift Network, The Sacred Path of Aloha, covers hoʻoponopono, HA breathing, chant, ceremony and ancestral remembrance.

courses.title: The Sacred Path of Aloha
courses.description: A seven-module self-paced video course in Hawaiian practices of aloha: hoʻoponopono (forgiveness and reconciliation), HA breathing, ancestral remembrance, chant and ceremony. Kumu Ramsay shows how these teachings can be lived day to day in relationship with yourself, others and the land.

courses.title: One-to-One Hoʻoponopono Session
courses.description: A private hoʻoponopono session with Kumu Ramsay, the Hawaiian process of reconciliation and forgiveness, booked directly online. Packages of three and small group sessions of up to five people can be arranged by email.

flags: Instagram, Facebook and X follower counts could not be read; his own YouTube channel is tiny and most of his video presence is on other channels (Unity Church of Hawaii, PBS Hawaiʻi, TEDx).
Most videos are on other channels (church talks, PBS and podcast interviews) where he is the main speaker; his own channel has only short Q&A clips.

The Sacred Path of Aloha sales page speaks of healing ancestral wounds, and its YouTube trailer is titled '...Ancient Hawaiian Wisdom for Healing Trauma'; kept because the course content is hoʻoponopono, breath, chant and ceremony, but a human should confirm.
One-to-one hoʻoponopono sessions are included as one offering because they are the main bookable service on his own site (alongside consulting and keynotes); price not shown.
City set to Honolulu from a PBS Hawaiʻi profile ('Ramsay Taum of Honolulu'); his site gives no address. He also teaches in-person immersions on the mainland (e.g. Arizona).
Also published on his site: kumu@leiofthepacific.com (site footer); wayofaloha@ is the address the contact page asks people to use.
The Shift Network lists a new live course starting December 2026 and a free event on 14 Nov 2026, but neither has a public page yet.
